newsitem.title: USA: Kewaunee nuclear plant unexpected problems found.
newsitem.headline: Kewaunee nuclear plant unexpected problems found.

text.p: Testing of the repairs of the steam generators at the Kewaunee (Wis.) nuclear plant has revealed unexpected problems, said Wisconsin Public Service, operator of the plant.
Wisconsin Public Service, a unit of WPS Resources Corp, said Thursday it will analyze the situation before deciding what action to take.
Plant manager Charlie Schrock said it was too early to predict if the original forecast of restarting the plant during the first quarter of 1997 will change.

Wisconsin Public Service has been repairing about 1,900 steam generator tubes by using a new laser welding process. Schrock said the latest test was to fill the steam generators with water and test for leaks. "We found several tubes with small leaks. Now we have to find out why," he said in a statement.
The plant's two steam generators have been in operation since 1994.

The company expects to receive permission from the Public Service Commission of Wisconsin this month for a temporary surcharge on customer bills to help pay for the additional cost of buying or generating electricity from other sources while the Kewaunee plant is shut down.
Wisconsin Public Service shares ownership of the plant with WPL Holdings Inc's Wisconsin Power & Light and Madison Gas & Electric Co.
